headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH MAGNET EXPORTS TO US DROP 21% IN AUGUST — EXPORT CONTROL THREAT PUTS CRITICAL MINERALS AT CENTER OF SEPT 24 TRUMP-XI SUMMIT
snippet: China's rare earth magnet exports to the US fell 21% month-over-month in August to just 512 tonnes — down 13% year-on-year — according to Chinese customs data published September 21. The sharp decline, which precedes the September 24 Trump-Xi summit in Washington, is being driven by exporters front-loading shipments before China's rare earth export control suspension expires November 10. Analysts warn that if China declines to renew or tighten controls at expiry, the supply shock to US defence and EV manufacturing would be immediate, giving Beijing asymmetric leverage in trade negotiations over Taiwan, AI technology, and tariffs.

headline: BANYAN GOLD RAISES $58M VIA LIFE OFFERING AND PRIVATE PLACEMENT — YUKON'S AURMAC PROJECT FULLY FUNDED FOR 2026-27 AT $2.00/SHARE
snippet: Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV: BYN) announced a $50M Listed Issuer Financing Exemption offering led by Canaccord Genuity at $2.00/share, running concurrently with a non-brokered $8M private placement at the same price — $58M in total, the largest single junior mining financing announced this week. Net proceeds advance the AurMac flagship project in Yukon's Na-Cho Nyäk Dun Traditional Territory (home to the Airstrip and Powerline Deposits), with closing targeted on or around September 29, 2026. At current gold prices above $4,370/oz, the AurMac project carries substantially improved economics versus the 2024 PEA assumptions.

headline: DLP RESOURCES COLLARS FIRST-EVER DRILL HOLE AT ESPERANZA PORPHYRY IN PERU — 3,000M PROGRAM TARGETS NEAR-SURFACE COPPER OXIDE AND MAIN CuAuMo BODY
snippet: DLP Resources (TSXV: DLP) collared its first hole at the Esperanza copper-gold-molybdenum porphyry project in southern Peru on September 20, commencing a 3,000m, 7-hole maiden diamond drill program. The program targets two overlapping geological settings: a near-surface copper oxide zone amenable to heap-leach processing and, at depth, the main porphyry copper-gold-molybdenum body. Esperanza is located in Peru's proven copper-porphyry belt adjacent to large producing operations; assay results are expected in Q4 2026.

headline: CORE LITHIUM PRODUCES FIRST SPODUMENE CONCENTRATE AT RESTARTED FINNISS — FIRST SHIPMENT TARGETED DECEMBER QUARTER 2026
snippet: Core Lithium (ASX: CXO) produced its first spodumene concentrate from the restarted Finniss Lithium Operation in the Northern Territory, meeting its target of achieving first production within the September Quarter 2026. The restart, backed by A$290M in financing from Glencore, InfraVia, and Nebari, represents the return of Australia's first new hard-rock lithium mine in a decade. First shipment is targeted for the December Quarter 2026; the milestone is significant as it confirms Finniss is operational even as spot lithium carbonate prices remain 65% above the 2025 cycle floor.

headline: OLYMPIO METALS COMMENCES MAIDEN DRILL AT JACKNIFE SILVER IN IDAHO — 1,500M PROGRAM TESTS 8.2Moz DISTRICT UNTOUCHED SINCE 2012
snippet: Olympio Metals (ASX: OLY) has commenced its first-ever drill program at the Jacknife Silver Project in Idaho's Lakeview Mining District — the first modern diamond drilling on the property since 2012. The 1,500m program targets structural corridors within an 8.2 million ounce historical silver district, with Scout Discoveries operating the drill on site. At current silver prices of $67/oz, the timing of new drill results in an established Idaho silver district carries significant market attention. Assays are expected before year-end.

headline: ANGLO-TECK COPPER MERGER AWAITS CHINA AND SOUTH KOREA CLEARANCE — $53B DEAL WINDOW SEPTEMBER 2026 TO MARCH 2027
snippet: The Anglo American–Teck Resources merger of equals — which would create one of the world's largest copper producers at roughly 1.2 million tonnes per year — has cleared Canadian, US, and EU regulatory hurdles and awaits only China and South Korea antitrust approval, with a closing window of September 2026 to March 2027. Shareholders of both companies approved the deal in December 2025 by votes exceeding 99%. The combined entity would carry approximately 70% copper exposure and US$800M in projected synergies; the outcome of this week's Trump-Xi summit could influence the pace of China's regulatory review.

headline: GATA'S CHRIS POWELL: GOVERNMENT GOLD SUPPRESSION IS LEGALLY AUTHORIZED — AND APPROACHING ITS PHYSICAL LIMIT AS EAST ABSORBS METAL
snippet: In a recent Money Metals podcast interview, GATA co-founder Chris Powell outlined how Western government intervention in gold markets is not a conspiracy theory but legally authorized under existing US statutes — and argues the suppression regime is approaching a physical limit as China, India, and Middle Eastern central banks continue absorbing metal at a pace that cannot be matched by paper gold supply expansion. With gold at $4,370 and physical-paper divergence now visible in lease rates and LBMA vault outflows, Powell's framework is gaining renewed mainstream attention after being dismissed for two decades.

headline: URANIUM MINERS REVERSE H1 LOSSES IN SEPTEMBER — NORTHSHORE GLOBAL INDEX UP 17%, JUNIORS UP 21.75% AS SPOT HOLDS ABOVE $82/LB
snippet: Uranium mining equities staged a sharp September reversal: the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index gained 17.01% month-to-date through September 19, with junior uranium miners up 21.75% — unwinding most of the H1 2026 underperformance documented by Sprott last week. Spot uranium held above $82/lb, up 8.05% in September, as the market digested simultaneous production-guidance cuts from both Cameco (19.5–21.5Mlb production vs. 29–32Mlb deliveries) and Kazatomprom (10% reduction, ~5Mlb removed from expected supply). Sprott's analysis frames the equity rerating as still incomplete given the structural supply deficit building under utility contract rollover schedules.

headline: EV RESOURCES REBRANDS AS ANTIMONY RESOURCES (ASX: ANT) TODAY — TECOMATLÁN PLANT IN MEXICO PROCESSING LIVE ANTIMONY ORE FROM CHINANTLA
snippet: EV Resources Limited officially rebranded as Antimony Resources Limited (ASX: ANT), effective September 21, 2026 — a rare ASX code change that signals a deliberate strategic pivot from battery metals to antimony, a critical mineral used in lead-acid batteries, flame retardants, and military-grade munitions. The company's Tecomatlán antimony processing plant in Guerrero, Mexico, is already operational, receiving ore from the adjacent Chinantla project. The rebrand underscores how capital is continuing to rotate within the critical minerals space as antimony prices benefit from China's tightening export controls across multiple commodity categories.

headline: RARE EARTHS FORCE TRUMP TO SOFTEN BEFORE XI SUMMIT — CHINA'S EXPORT CONTROL LEVERAGE IS CONSTRAINING US NEGOTIATING POSTURE ON TAIWAN AND AI
snippet: A US News & World Report analysis published September 21 argues that China's stranglehold on rare earth refining — roughly 85% of global capacity — is visibly moderating the Trump administration's rhetoric ahead of the September 24 Washington summit, constraining the US position on Taiwan, AI chip exports, and critical minerals supply chains simultaneously. With China's export control suspension expiring November 10, Beijing holds a credible threat that does not require action to be effective: the mere uncertainty is forcing Washington to negotiate. The piece identifies MP Materials, USA Rare Earth, and Lynas as the equities that benefit most from either a breakdown (premium on non-Chinese supply) or a structured agreement (certainty of Western investment).
